item.title: From football to the Drua: Boselawa credits dad and faith for his rugby journey

item.content:encoded:
From playing football throughout his school years to only taking up rugby at 19, Kavekini Karl Boselawa’s journey to becoming a Senior Development Player has been driven by faith, perseverance and the unwavering support of his family, especially his father.

Boselawa says rugby was not always the path he thought he would take, as he played football throughout primary and high school and only played touch rugby with the boys in his village during school holidays.

It was not until he was 19 and studying at university that he played rugby for the first time.

Boselawa attended Nadrala Sangam, Sigatoka Methodist and later spent three years at Fiji National University.

He says completing his education was important to him, and he finished university before deciding to seriously pursue rugby.

That decision has now paid off, with Boselawa saying receiving his official offer to become a Senior Development Player was an emotional moment that initially left him in disbelief.

He says the first thing that came to mind when he received the news was, “What?!”, adding he was excited, happy and thankful to God for the opportunity.

Behind his journey has been the strong influence of his father , whom Boselawa calls his “Tou”.

Boselawa says his father has had the biggest influence on him, both as a man and throughout his rugby journey.

He also says his father is a former rugby player who played centre, fullback and wing, the same positions Boselawa plays , and has been able to share his rugby experience and guidance with his son.

Boselawa says one of the biggest lessons his father has taught him is the importance of putting God first in everything he does and trusting that everything else will follow.

His father says the family is extremely proud of Kave and thanked him, his mother and their entire family for helping him reach the milestone.

He says it was also a special moment for the family to have the Drua visit their home as Boselawa begins the next chapter of his rugby journey.

He says they give all the glory to God for the opportunity and milestone.

item.title: Tailevu Rugby celebrates Rewa win by giving back to Nakelo District School
item.description: The players and team officials took part in the clean-up following their Skipper Provincial Cup victory over their neighbours. Tailevu Rugby says the initiative was an opportunity to give back to Nakelo District School, which has supported the union for decades.
item.content:encoded:
The players and team officials took part in the clean-up following their Skipper Provincial Cup victory over their neighbours.

Tailevu Rugby says the initiative was an opportunity to give back to Nakelo District School, which has supported the union for decades.

The school has provided its grounds as one of Tailevu Rugby's home venues for the Skipper Cup and Marama Cup competitions.

The union says while victories on the field are important, it also has a responsibility to serve the communities that continue to support the team.

Ministry of Environment and Climate Change has also commended the players and officials for the initiative.

Minister for Environment Lynda Tabuya says the players have demonstrated that leadership extends beyond the rugby field.

Tabuya describes the initiative as civic pride in action, saying sporting teams can use their influence to serve communities and encourage people to care for their surroundings.

Meanwhile, the Fresh Choice Tailevu Rugby women's side also had plenty to celebrate after recording a dominant victory over Rewa in the Marama Championship.

Tailevu women's player Ana Sassen says their success came from having the strength and knowledge to not only play rugby, but to play smart rugby.

Sassen thanked God for the victory and also acknowledged those who continue to support the team.

Tailevu Rugby says its message remains that rugby is about more than winning games, and includes serving communities, supporting schools and building relationships that can last for generations.

item.title: Savea ruled out of final Test against Springboks
item.description: Inspirational New Zealand captain Ardie Savea will miss the All Blacks' final Test against South Africa after suffering a shoulder injury in this morning's 29-24 defeat to the Springboks. The 32-year-old was forced from the field nine minutes before half-time in a major blow to the All Blacks, who now trail 2-1 in the four-Test series.
item.content:encoded:
Inspirational New Zealand captain Ardie Savea will miss the All Blacks' final Test against South Africa after suffering a shoulder injury in this morning's 29-24 defeat to the Springboks.

The 32-year-old was forced from the field nine minutes before half-time in a major blow to the All Blacks, who now trail 2-1 in the four-Test series.

Savea had scored two tries before his injury, but his departure allowed South Africa to gain greater control as they went on to secure a bruising victory at Soccer City.

All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie confirmed after the match that Savea would not travel with the team to the United States for the fourth Test .

The fourth Test will be played in Baltimore, USA next Sunday, with the All Blacks needing a victory to level the series.

The All Blacks will now have to regroup without their captain as they look to force a series decider with victory in Baltimore.

item.title: Suva qualifies for BOG semi-finals despite 2-1 loss to Nasinu
item.description: Global Care Suva has secured its place in the semi-finals of the Extra Supermarket Battle of the Giants despite suffering a 2-1 defeat to Nasinu at 4R Stadium in Govind Park, Ba. This result eliminates Navua from semi-final contention, while Nasinu will await the outcome of the match between Labasa and Navua.
item.content:encoded:
Global Care Suva has secured its place in the semi-finals of the Extra Supermarket Battle of the Giants despite suffering a 2-1 defeat to Nasinu at 4R Stadium in Govind Park, Ba.

This result eliminates Navua from semi-final contention, while Nasinu will await the outcome of the match between Labasa and Navua.

Labasa needs a 3-0 victory to qualify for the semi-finals.

Nasinu’s Paul Francis opened the scoring in the 18th minute before Suva striker Gagame Feni equalised just three minutes later.

Nasinu captain Billy Afi, who is originally from the Solomon Islands, then scored the decisive goal to give his side a 2-1 victory.

Despite the loss, Suva’s earlier results have given them enough points to qualify for the semi-finals.

Meanwhile, Tagimoucia Nadi is currently playing Stratum/PPCL Rewa in another BOG encounter.

In the upcoming matches, Blue Gas Navua will face defending champions Extra Supermarket Labasa at 3.30pm, while hosts Dayal’s Steel Ba will take on Khelvin Engineering Lautoka at 5.30pm.
